name: geometry-unescaped-ampersand
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, then hand-edited in Notepad to paste a Google Fonts @import
story: The designer pasted a Google Fonts @import into the exported file's <style> block straight off the Google Fonts page, ampersand and all - and an ampersand in XML starts an entity reference, so the document stopped being well-formed at that character.
idioms: a RAW & inside <style> text content (?family=Bebas+Neue&display=swap), which XML reads as the start of an entity reference and rejects with "EntityRef: expecting ';'"
the <style> content NOT wrapped in CDATA - Illustrator writes it as plain text, which is what leaves the paste exposed

an otherwise perfectly ordinary Illustrator Internal CSS export around it: Generator comment, version="1.1" id="Layer_1" x="0px" y="0px", enable-background, xml:space="preserve", .stN classes with one property each, <text transform="matrix(...)">
the damage is one character on one line, and everything before and after it is valid
whyThisMatters: The corpus had no refusing fixture at all - the sidecar format has carried an "accepted": false branch and a refusalAbout field since it was written, and not one file exercised them, so the entire refusal road was unmeasured. This is the refusal a student is most likely to actually meet, because pasting a webfont import is what people do when type looks wrong and an unescaped ampersand is what a paste from a URL bar contains. The file is genuinely unimportable and should stay that way; what is being measured is whether the door names the character and the place, or says "damaged, or not an SVG at all" and sends someone back to Illustrator to re-export a file that was never the problem. It pairs with effects-css-import-webfont, which is the same edit with the ampersand escaped.
